subject: Checkout blocked window — SLA assertion and RCA plan request
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@brightcart.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@brightcart.com
Date: Fri, 8 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Checkout failure window — requesting SLA credit and RCA

Marcus,

We saw a service-unreachable condition that blocked customer checkouts this morning. Between 08:41:20 and 09:02:12 PST several checkout API calls for our fastlane path (/v1/generate and /v1/chat) returned 503/connection errors and retries failed — it impacted ~8% of checkouts during that 20-minute interval and caused a noticeable revenue drop.

Attached a screenshot of the checkout error and a small sample of request IDs we captured. Ops has also exported traces (linked) but we need Redwood to:

- Confirm the precise unreachable/503 window you observe on the platform side (timestamps in UTC preferred)
- Provide an eligibility assessment for SLA credit and the calculation method you will apply
- Share an estimated timeline for a postmortem (RCAs and mitigating actions)

This is blocking our execs from closing the loop with merchants — please treat as urgent.

--
Samantha Lee
Director, Site Reliability
BrightCart
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@brightcart.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 8 Mar 2029 09:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Checkout failure window — requesting SLA credit and RCA

Thanks Samantha — really sorry you hit this. I’ve looped in Grace (CS) and Aditya (sales) so we can coordinate the remedy and communications.

Immediate plan:
- Engineering will validate the platform-level availability window and pull raw traces/host metrics.
- We’ll produce a preliminary downtime tally (UTC) and an initial assessment of SLA eligibility within 4 business hours.
- If eligible, we’ll propose a credit calculation and confirm timeline for issuing it.

Can you attach the sample request-ids (full request-id strings) and the transaction ids for affected checkouts? That will speed the trace-join. I’ve requested raw traces from our serving cluster and asked for a bundle to be attached to this thread.

I’ll follow up with an engineering note shortly.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha@brightcart.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 8 Mar 2029 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Checkout failure window — requesting SLA credit and RCA

On Fri, Mar 8, 2029 at 09:26 AM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Can you attach the sample request-ids (full request-id strings) and the transaction ids for affected checkouts?

Thanks — I pulled the serving traces and request logs. Summary of findings:

- Observed RPC failures from our north-virginia availability set between 2029-03-08T16:41:19Z and 2029-03-08T16:59:56Z (UTC) for the BrightCart tenant route.
- Root cause appears to be a short GPU host eviction event that caused 3 worker processes to restart; during the restart window we saw a small backlog which produced 503 responses for traffic routed to those hosts.
- We calculated the total interval where BrightCart observed client-visible failures as 18 minutes 37 seconds (start/end times above). Attached is a trace bundle (brightcart_kv_traces_20290308.tar.gz) and a trimmed host metric CSV for the node restarts.

SLA credit eligibility note: per the contract (section 4.2) an availability gap that results from host preemption is covered as an outage if it results in client-visible 5xx responses across the tenant route. Given the observed 503 spike and the measured window (18m37s) BrightCart qualifies for a pro-rata credit under our standard SLA.

Proposed next steps:
1) We will produce a formal credit calculation using BrightCart’s monthly committed spend and the 18m37s outage window. Expect a draft credit offset within 48 hours.
2) Ownered postmortem: I’ll schedule a deep-dive and produce an RCA note (root cause, timeline, remediation) within 7 business days.
3) Immediate mitigation we’ll apply: pinning the tenant routing to healthy host pool for 72 hours and adding a short-term scaling headroom to reduce preemption risk during peak checkout windows.

Attachments referenced: brightcart_kv_traces_20290308.tar.gz, host-restarts-20290308.csv

Let me know if you want the credit calculation to be delivered to your finance contact directly (I can include the math and the affected invoice lines).

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Engineering — Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@brightcart.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 8 Mar 2029 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Checkout failure window — requesting SLA credit and RCA

Samantha,

Thanks for the sample IDs and for your patience. Per Soojin’s analysis above we’ve confirmed an 18m37s client-visible outage (2029-03-08T16:41:19Z to 2029-03-08T16:59:56Z).

Action items we’ll execute now:
- Engineering will prepare the formal credit calculation and share a draft with you and your finance team in 48 hours. If you’d like us to route the credit item directly to ops-billing@brightcart.com please confirm.
- We’ll publish a postmortem (RCA, timeline, and remediation work) in 7 business days and share the doc link once available.
- Grace will follow up with a short customer-facing note for merchant comms and a small goodwill offer to affected merchants (proposal attached as sla-claim-form-BRG-4572.pdf).

If BrightCart agrees to the proposed path, please reply with the finance contact for issuing the credit and whether you want any changes to the postmortem cadence.

We apologize again for the impact — we’ll treat this with priority and keep you updated.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
